article_title: Fostering EFL Learners' Reading Comprehension: Animation Film Technique
citation: Asefeh Torabian, Massoud Tajadini. (2017). Fostering EFL Learners' Reading Comprehension: Animation Film Technique. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 8(2). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.8n.2p.55
title: Dual Coding Theory as the framework for animation-supported reading comprehension
description: The study's stated theoretical framework is Paivio's Dual Coding Theory, which "identifies two modes of processing information: imagery and language". It holds that verbal and pictorial memory are "two interlinked but discrete long-term memory systems", so concrete language can be stored both verbally and as imagery, and learners using both modes simultaneously gain better comprehension. The authors adopt it because animation films supply imagery alongside story text, establishing a basis for EFL reading-comprehension learning.
requirements: Learning material must pair verbal content with imagery so both processing modes are engaged
target_learners: pre-intermediate EFL learners
target_learning_goals: reading comprehension of short stories
examples: The experimental group watched 60 minutes of animation film across the three-month course, divided into 6-7 minutes per session, alongside the story books.

article_title: The Effect of BBC World Clips with and without Subtitles on Intermediate EFL Learners' Vocabulary Development
citation: Effat Heidari Sirmandi, Sedigheh Abbasnasab Sardareh. (2016). The Effect of BBC World Clips With and Without Subtitles on Intermediate EFL Learners' Vocabulary Development. Malaysian Online Journal of Educational Sciences. https://www.moj-es.net
title: Dual coding theory as the theoretical basis for bimodal subtitling effects on vocabulary learning
description: The article grounds its expectation that subtitled films aid vocabulary learning in Paivio's dual coding theory, which "introduced through this theory to develop learnt material: verbal association and visual imagery". The verbal and imagery systems are described as independent subsystems, and in subtitled films three independent systems (including two verbal systems in bilingual situations) interconnect simultaneously, which the authors say "might cause better processing and recall due to image and translation effects". description: The article draws on Paivio's (1971) dual coding theory, which proposes that information can be simultaneously represented by pictures and words, activating two functionally autonomous but interconnected coding systems: visual and verbal codes. It also draws on multiple-channel theory (Hsia, 1971), which proposes that comprehension increases as learners interact with any combination of different available sensory channels. Captioned videos leverage both theories by providing simultaneous exposure to spoken language, printed text and visual information.

title: Dual-path serial mediation model of academic foundation on postgraduate exam success
description: The article proposes and validates a serial multiple mediation model in which academic foundation influences postgraduate entrance exam success through two indirect pathways: one operating sequentially through psychological state then behavioral engagement, and one operating through psychological state alone. The model is grounded in Ecosystem Theory and Self-Determination Theory, which hold that "academic achievement is jointly shaped by the interaction of individual inherent characteristics, behavioral engagement, and external environmental factors." Moderating variables such as motivation level and personality traits were not modeled

Medical students preparing for competitive admissions

description: The Dunning-Kruger effect is the educational psychological phenomenon whereby "limited knowledge causes individuals to overestimate their competence and underestimate others’, leading to poor self-assessment and unrecognized incompetence". constraints: The article notes statistical explanations (hard-easy effect, regression to the mean, better-than-average approach, measurement error, boundary restrictions) compete with the metacognitive account, though recent literature underscores the metacognitive explanation

citation: Krumm Ilana Roberts MD, Miles Matthew C. MD, MEd, FCCP, Clay Alison MD, Carlos II W. Graham MD, Adamson Rosemary MBBS. (2021). Making Effective Educational Videos for Clinical Teaching. Chest. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chest.2021.09.015
title: Dual-channel processing and cognitive load theory as the basis for educational video design
description: The article grounds its video-design recommendations in two overlapping theories. Dual-channel processing holds that multimedia content is processed by working memory via separate audio and visual channels: "The dual-channel principle states that humans can process visual and auditory/written information simultaneously." Cognitive load theory adds that "each channel has a limited capacity to process information," and overload inhibits learning. Extraneous load from distractions reduces capacity available for relevant information. The article uses these theories to justify concise narration, complementary images, segmentation, and avoiding distractions.
requirements: Video design must respect the limited capacity of each working memory channel and avoid extraneous material that is not the focus of the video

target_learning_goals: understanding and retention of clinical concepts and procedures from video-based instruction
examples: The lung slide videos use simple slides with short annotations and arrows so narration and images take advantage of both channels without extraneous load

article_title: Improving Preschoolers' Arithmetic through Number Magnitude Training: The Impact of Non-Symbolic and Symbolic Training.
citation: Honoré Nastasya, Noël Marie-Pascale. (2016). Improving Preschoolers' Arithmetic through Number Magnitude Training: The Impact of Non-Symbolic and Symbolic Training. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0166685
title: Dual-representation view of numerical cognition
description: The dual-representation view holds that symbolic and non-symbolic numbers activate distinct magnitude representations: "non-symbolic numbers activate the ANS and symbolic numbers activate an exact representation of numbers; the latter is the root of mathematical learning and can refine the ANS." It contrasts with the unique-representation view in which the ANS represents both formats and underlies all numerical learning. The article tests the two views with a training design and concludes its results support the dual-representation view, since only symbolic training improved arithmetic.
requirements: Symbolic numbers must be distinguished from non-symbolic numerosities when measuring or training magnitude processing
constraints: The view does not reject the role of the ANS; once exact symbolic representations are built, connections between them and the ANS are established
target_learners: preschool children prior to formal mathematics instruction
target_learning_goals: numerical magnitude representation
exact arithmetic
examples: The article contrasted two otherwise identical training programs differing only in stimulus format (dot collections vs Arabic numbers) to test the two views' predictions

title: Duesseldorf List of Complaints: 123 complaint items linking multidisciplinary diseases to clinical practice training
description: The Duesseldorf Curriculum is built on learning with patient complaint items: "For this educational format, 123 complaint items were defined and their compatibility with diseases from various disciplines was tested." The list was synthesized from the Dundee task list, the German Catalog of Learning Objectives (GK2-2009) and the Dutch Blue Print 2009, revised by directors and lecturers of 44 clinics and institutes, and passed by the Faculty Council. Complaint handling is largely independent of the health care environment, while underlying diseases vary with setting.
requirements: The list had to be extensive enough to link to all diseases relevant for medical studies across disciplines, yet limited enough to provide practical use in clinical practice training
constraints: Reasons for consultation predominantly in outpatient and primary care, such as advisory services, screening and vaccination, were also included
target_learners: medical students in their 3rd, 4th and 5th year of study
target_learning_goals: clinical thinking and action
differential diagnostic and therapeutical procedures
integration of basic-science knowledge into clinical cases
examples: Students are requested to elaborate at least 80% of the 123 complaints and reasons for consultation during the overall 40 weeks of practice blocks
